name: Commercial platforms, DPP service providers and sector programmes
scope_note: Covers (1) about 30 commercial and open platforms that publicly describe a DPP technical approach, (2) the DPP service provider role in Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 and the status of its delegated act, (3) sector rules and pilots for batteries, construction products, toys, iron and steel, textiles, electronics, tyres and furniture, and (4) literature from 2021 to 2026. Leaves out the text of every EN, ISO, IEC and DIN document (bibliographic metadata only). No live DPP system, resolver, registry, connector, wallet or ledger node was contacted. All vendor statements are secondary_only. Several vendor pages state few technical facts; those gaps are recorded as 'not stated', not filled in.
summary: A platform-based DPP implementation is a hosted or self-hosted service that stores passport data for an economic operator, issues identifiers and data carriers, and serves different views to different audiences. Data enters from ERP, PLM or PIM systems, supplier questionnaires, or lifecycle events (often EPCIS 2.0). The passport store sits behind a REST API with OAuth 2.0 or OIDC, and exposes a public view and restricted views. Identifiers are most often GS1 Digital Link URLs printed as QR codes; the resolver redirects or negotiates content by headers. Variants add W3C verifiable credentials with DID documents (did:web), hash anchoring on a ledger (IOTA, Hyperledger Fabric, public chains, NFT tokens), or a Catena-X dataspace where Eclipse Dataspace Connectors and a digital twin registry carry the data. Under Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 the economic operator must make a back-up copy available through an independent DPP service provider (Art. 10(4)), and the passport may be stored by the operator or by such providers (Art. 11, first subparagraph, point (c)). A provider that stores or processes the data may not sell or reuse it beyond the service (Art. 11, second subparagraph). The Commission may set provider requirements and a certification scheme by delegated act (Art. 11, third subparagraph); on 2026-10-19 the Commission DPP page still lists that act under both Q2 2027 and Q3 2027, and no adopted act was located. The DPP registry (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778) lists verified service providers and checks the back-up link at registration. Batteries have the earliest binding date (18 February 2027); toys (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Arts 19 to 23, applying from 1 August 2030) and construction products (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, Arts 75 to 80, through a delegated act planned for Q2 2027) have their own DPP articles, while iron and steel (Q4 2026), textiles, aluminium and tyres (Q3 to Q4 2027), furniture (2028) and mattresses (2029) wait for ESPR delegated acts. Sector pilots (13 CIRPASS-2 pilots, Trace4Value, Battery Pass and BatteryPass-Ready, Catena-X, Cir4Fun) mostly describe goals; the concrete technical details are QR plus GS1 identifiers for textiles and construction, RFID plus a tyre dataspace for tyres, federated platforms for electronics, and AAS or Catena-X aspect models for batteries. For a black-box conformance engine the most testable surface is: identifier shapes at model, batch and item level, resolver and content negotiation behavior, role-based field visibility, signature or proof verification, version links, the back-up redirect, and registry consistency; most of these need capabilities that are interface_only today.

maturity.spec_status: No technical standard or adopted law fixes the platform architecture. The ESPR DPP service provider delegated act is not adopted (listed for Q2 2027 and Q3 2027 on the Commission DPP page read on 2026-10-19). No ESPR product-group delegated act that makes a DPP mandatory was located. The DPP registry operates (Commission pages: since 2026-07-20; Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 in force since 2026-08-06 per the prior record). Open building blocks are mature enough to cite by version (GS1 Digital Link 1.7.0, GS1-Conformant Resolver 1.2.1, AAS API v3.2, Catena-X CX-0143 v1.3 and CX-0160 v1.0). Vendor platforms are proprietary; only a few publish an API contract.

maturity.adoption_evidence: Vendor-reported only: atma.io claims more than 30 billion items on its cloud; Arianee reports 40 to 50+ brands and 3.1 to 3.4 million passports (two pages disagree); Circulor reports 150 million batteries traced; Minespider reports 6 million batches traced in 2026. None is independently verified. Independent evidence is thinner: CIRPASS-2 runs 13 lighthouse pilots in four value chains; the Trace4Value textile pilot put first garments with a DPP on the market in January 2024 (GS1 Sweden case page); the Cofinity-X marketplace lists several Catena-X certified DPP solutions. The literature review of 225 studies (10.1007/s43615-026-00927-x) finds most work conceptual with limited empirical validation. As of 2026-10-19 no product category has a binding DPP delegated act under the ESPR.
maturity.regulatory_alignment: Regulation (EU) 2024/1781, Art. 2(30) defines the unique product identifier as a string that also enables a web link to the passport; Art. 2(32) defines the DPP service provider as an independent third party authorised by the operator; Art. 10(1) sets carrier, identifier, open-standard, no-vendor-lock-in and personal-data rules; Art. 10(4) requires a back-up copy through a service provider; Art. 11 sets design requirements (interoperability, access, storage by the operator or providers, links to earlier passports, availability after insolvency, restricted update rights, authentication and integrity, security and privacy). Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 sets the registry (Art. 3 point (f): list of verified service providers). Regulation (EU) 2025/2509 (toys), Arts 19 to 23 and Regulation (EU) 2024/3110 (construction), Arts 75 to 80 repeat the same design requirements in their own sector text. Battery passport duties come from Regulation (EU) 2023/1542; the Commission FAQ says that regulation does not define a service provider as a separate actor (prior record). The Art. 77(9) battery access-rights implementing act was not located.

L01_unique_identifiers.mechanism: Platforms issue identifiers at model, batch or item level and link each to a passport URL. Observed shapes: (1) GS1 Digital Link URL https://<operator-or-vendor-domain>/01/<GTIN-14>[/22/<consumer product variant>][/10/<lot>][/21/<serial>], reported for Arianee, Circularise (GTIN plus serial), TrusTrace, atma.io, Kezzler, EON, Digimarc and the Trace4Value pilot. The GS1 syntax puts the primary key first, then qualifiers in fixed class-to-instance order (variant, lot, serial); any qualifier may be omitted but the order of the rest must hold; serial is optional; GTIN-8/12/13 are zero-padded to 14 digits; data attributes go in the query string; the canonical form uses host id.gs1.org (GS1 Digital Link 1.7.0). (2) DID-based: Spherity passport DIDs of the form did:web:<api-host>:did-registry:<passport-id>, and a battery example did:web:<domain>/battery/<UUID> with the issuer as did:web:<company-host>. (3) Catena-X: Business Partner Number plus manufacturer part id and digital twin ids in a Digital Twin Registry (BPN and part ids are not described on the pages read; the battery example mentions a unique battery id and a VIN). (4) NFT token ids (Arianee protocol; the docs read did not state the id format). (5) EON uses GS1 Digital Link for GTIN products and its own resolver format for products without a GTIN. (6) EPC URNs from EPCIS that a toolkit converts to and from Digital Link (OpenEPCIS). (7) RFID memory identifiers for tyres and apparel tags (atma.io dual RFID plus QR in pilot PA4; Michelin pilot uses RFID). (8) Serialized secure QR codes with a changeable redirect (Scantrust, Circularise). Internal handles that are not carrier identifiers: Circularise disclosure record ids (sample pattern with a prefix and suffix) and Arianee REST ids in /v2/passports/{id}.

L01_unique_identifiers.observable_black_box: The text decoded from the carrier; whether it is an http(s) URL; the path segments; whether the URL resolves at the stated granularity; whether the identifier is a DID or a token id instead of a URL; whether the same item identifier gives the same passport as the model-level identifier.
L01_unique_identifiers.law_delta: Adopted law requires only that the identifier enables a web link and is persistent; it names no scheme for ESPR products. Annex III first paragraph point (c) lists a GTIN as an optional data element (prior record). The GS1 Digital Link forms with no serial, with a lot, or with a variant are valid under the GS1 syntax; the engine's identifier.parse accepts only the /01/<GTIN>/21/<serial> form, so batch-level and model-level URLs from platforms would be reported as syntax errors even where valid.

L02_data_carriers.mechanism: QR codes are the common carrier on every platform read. Variants: GS1 Digital Link QR; dynamic or serialized QR with a redirect URL that can change after printing (Circularise, Scantrust); secure QR with a copy detection pattern in the code center, authenticated by a phone camera (Scantrust claim); dual RFID plus QR tags that each supply-chain actor scans to update the passport (atma.io pilot PA4); RFID tyre tags (Michelin pilot PC1, via an ISO tyre identification standard whose number the pilot page does not give); NFC tags and woven or printed labels (EON); QR codes inside garments applied by a trims supplier (Kezzler pilot PA2). Platforms also generate batches of carriers: Arianee endpoint POST /v2/qr-codes/batch produces GS1 Digital Link QR codes. Law side: the carrier must be physically on the product, packaging or accompanying documents (Art. 10(1)(b)); for toys the carrier goes on the toy or a label, else packaging or documents, visible before purchase including distance sales, with one carrier serving all applicable EU law (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 19(7) and (8)); for construction products the carrier is affixed as Art. 18(2)(g) requires (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, Art. 77(1)(b)).

L02_data_carriers.observable_black_box: A QR image file (decode text, error correction level is not graded by the engine); for NFC and RFID a tag dump, which the engine cannot read today; the redirect chain behind the printed URL.
L02_data_carriers.law_delta: Law fixes where the carrier must be and that it links to the passport; it does not choose QR, RFID or NFC for ESPR products. Anti-counterfeit print patterns and RFID tag standards are vendor or sector choices, not legal requirements in the texts read.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.mechanism: Four exchange styles appear. (1) Web resolution: the carrier URL is requested over HTTPS; a GS1-conformant resolver redirects to the default link unless the request supplies better matching data (query linkType=<CURIE>, where gs1: expands to https://ref.gs1.org/voc/; Accept-Language for language variants). Accept: application/linkset+json returns the RFC 9264 linkset without redirect; application/ld+json returns JSON-LD; text/html or no Accept header returns an HTML page with the linkset embedded. Status codes: 300 when several links of one type tie, 400 for an invalid identifier, 404 for a valid identifier with no data or an unknown link type; a resolver must not use 200 for an error. A resolver hosts a description file at /.well-known/gs1resolver (RFC 8615). A redirect to another resolver carries a Link header with rel gs1:handledBy besides Location (GS1-Conformant Resolver 1.2.1). (2) Vendor REST with JSON or JSON-LD, OAuth 2.0 bearer tokens, webhooks and bulk file exchange (EON, Arianee). (3) EPCIS 2.0 capture and query for lifecycle events (Digimarc beta API, Kezzler, atma.io, EON, Arianee claims). (4) Dataspace exchange: in Catena-X an Eclipse Dataspace Connector publishes data offers, the consumer discovers the partner endpoint, negotiates a contract and pulls the submodel; Industry Core Hub orchestrates these steps. Wallet-to-wallet exchange with DIDs is an alternative; the Spherity battery write-up says it did not use an Eclipse connector because that conflicted with wallet-to-wallet communication. Back-up redirection is a separate protocol question: the CIRPASS-2 options paper compares five designs (Commission-run fallback registry of back-up links, Commission-managed subdomains with DNS redirect, Commission-run central redirect, agency takeover of domains of exited operators, and a two-URL scheme with a fixed mapping); one contributor notes that option 1 (the fallback registry) is the one recommended in the earlier CIRPASS architecture (version 1.9), and the paper lists each contributor's pros and cons without choosing.

L03_data_exchange_protocols.observable_black_box: HTTP status, Location and Link headers, Content-Type and body for each Accept value; the redirect chain length; behavior for a valid identifier with no data (404 versus 200); whether a description file exists at /.well-known/gs1resolver; for dataspaces, the catalog and negotiation messages (not observable without a connector).
L03_data_exchange_protocols.law_delta: Art. 10(1)(d) requires open standards, an interoperable format and transfer through an open interoperable data exchange network without vendor lock-in; Art. 11 point (a) requires interoperability with other passports. No adopted law names GS1 resolver, EPCIS or EDC; the batch back-up redirect mechanism is not fixed by law (open design question).

L04_apis_lifecycle_searchability.mechanism: Commercial API (Arianee Enterprise, vendor page): REST v2 documented in OpenAPI 3.0 with POST /v2/passports (create), GET /v2/passports/{id} (read), PUT /v2/passports/{id} (update), DELETE /v2/passports/{id} (delete after archiving), POST /v2/passports/{id}/events (lifecycle event), POST /v2/passports/{id}/ownership-transfer, GET /v2/passports/{id}/compliance-status, POST /v2/qr-codes/batch, and GET/POST /v2/webhooks; authentication by API key or OpenID Connect with JWT, optional IP allow list. EON: REST read and write, webhooks, bulk files, OpenAPI documentation, OAuth 2.0 bearer header. Open implementations: Eclipse BaSyx Go has a DPP API service (CRUD, versioned lookup, PostgreSQL storage per the OpenDPP catalogue entry) next to AAS registries and repositories that follow AAS API v3.2; open-dpp has a REST API behind a cloud endpoint; the CIRPASS-2 mock registry exposes HTTP endpoints with OIDC roles admin, eo and eu (prior record); the CIRPASS-2 data extractor fills a search-key cache. Registry API: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778 Art. 3 point (b) provides an API to register passports and receive registry information. Most vendor pages do not publish endpoint contracts; atma.io's product API documentation is login-gated according to a third-party catalogue.

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.mechanism: Data models in use: (a) AAS submodel templates from IDTA (IDTA 02099-1 Digital Product Passport metadata; IDTA 02035 Digital Battery Passport parts 1 to 7, versions 1.0.0 to 1.0.1 per the Catena-X EcoPass page) serialized as AAS JSON or AASX; (b) Catena-X semantic aspect models in the Semantic Aspect Meta Model, with identifiers such as io.catenax.generic.digital_product_passport 6.1.0, io.catenax.battery.battery_pass 6.1.0 and io.catenax.material.chemical_material_passport 3.0.0, governed by Catena-X standards CX-0143 v1.3 (optional baseline for ESPR products) and CX-0160 v1.0 (mandatory battery passport); (c) BatteryPass-Ready data model v2.0 and longlist (Excel), a machine-readable model of elements, types and codelists aligned with Regulation (EU) 2023/1542; (d) CIRPASS-2 ontologies: a CORE ontology with sector modules; the battery umbrella 0.4.0 DRAFT uses namespace https://w3id.org/eudpp/battery# and nine thematic modules plus SHACL shapes and access-tier view files; a tyre example ontology (eto.owl); an initial textile ontology led by GS1 with Graphwise; (e) UNTP credential vocabularies in JSON-LD with W3C verifiable credentials (version 0.7.0 'Pilots'); (f) GS1 EPCIS 2.0 event model with JSON-LD binding; (g) community JSON schemas such as TracePass (913 fields over 12 categories, as listed in the OpenDPP catalogue) and TracePath open schemas; (h) vendor schemas: Arianee Identity, NFT, Message and Event schemas and JSON-LD with Schema.org; the TrusTrace Trace4Value textile protocol with 126 data points in 9 categories (search excerpt, secondary). A CIRPASS-2 deliverable on AAS and RDF interoperability exists (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.19885637, title listed on the results page; content not read).

L05_system_interoperability_data_models.law_delta: Law (Art. 10(1)(d)) asks for open standards and machine-readable, structured, searchable data; the binding data set per product group will come from delegated acts, which do not yet exist for ESPR products. L06_storage_archiving_persistence.mechanism: Hosting models: vendor-hosted SaaS (Arianee on Google Cloud with MongoDB Atlas in selectable EU regions France, Germany, Sweden, optional UK; Siemens Battery Passport as SaaS in licence tiers; Circulor on Oracle Cloud Infrastructure with Hyperledger Fabric; IBCT Infirium with dedicated server resources per customer and optional on-premises or DMZ deployment), self-hosted open source (open-dpp Docker Compose; Industry Core Hub Helm and local umbrella; BaSyx Go with PostgreSQL 16 and optional read replicas), data kept at the manufacturer with only hashes on a ledger (Digimarc and IOTA; Spherity battery write-up says data are not uploaded to central systems). Back-up: law requires a back-up copy of the passport through a DPP service provider when the product is placed on the market (Art. 10(4)); toys repeat this in Art. 19(13); construction requires a back-up system run by service providers (Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, Art. 75(2)(f)). The registry checks the link to the back-up (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, recital 16). Retention: toys keep the passport 10 years after placing on the market (Art. 19(2)(g)); construction requires the system to stay accessible 25 years after the last matching product and each passport at least 10 years, unless disproportionately costly (Art. 75(2)(i)); Art. 11 point (e) of the ESPR requires availability for the period in delegated acts, including after insolvency. The CIRPASS-2 service provider response separates 'back-up operators' from other providers and lists services such as hosting with redirect, archiving for operators that left the EU market and provider switching; it asks for service levels, recovery time and recovery point objectives. Vendors claim ISO/IEC 27001 certification (Circularise, Spherity, Kezzler, Minespider, Scantrust, iPoint) and SOC 2 Type II (Arianee, Spherity); these are organisation certificates, not proof of passport availability.

L06_storage_archiving_persistence.observable_black_box: Whether a back-up location is declared and reachable; response after the primary is down (only on a controlled fixture); version history; archive or inactive status; response time; the retention period stated in the document.
L06_storage_archiving_persistence.law_delta: Retention periods are in sector law (toys 10 years; construction 25 and 10 years) and ESPR delegated acts later; the ESPR text leaves the period to delegated acts. Law does not state availability service levels, recovery objectives or the activation procedure of the back-up when an operator fails.

L07_access_rights_security_confidentiali.mechanism: Observed mechanisms: field-level permissions per audience with disclosure groups Public, Partners, Internal and Carbon and per-field Hidden, Read or Edit (Circularise consumer-passport page); SAML single sign-on (Circularise); OAuth 2.0 with JWT, API key or OpenID Connect, optional IP allow list, audit logging of every API call (Arianee); role-based access with audiences such as regulator, retailer, consumer (EON); role-based visibility inside a Hyperledger Fabric network (Circulor); verifiable credentials for selective sharing, with access for authorities and persons with legitimate interest (Spherity; its battery write-up says non-public attributes need user authentication and the mechanism is not standardised, with a mock login); EDC contract policies carrying ownership and access rights (Catena-X); OIDC roles admin, eo and eu on the CIRPASS-2 mock registry (prior record); the CIRPASS-2 battery ontology ships view files for public, legitimate-interest and authority tiers (battery-view-public.ttl, battery-view-legitimate-interest.ttl, battery-view-authorities.ttl, battery-access-tiers.ttl). Zero-knowledge proofs for selective claims are claimed by Circularise (patent-pending 'smart questioning', secondary). Law: ESPR Art. 11 points (b) and (f) tie access and update rights to the delegated act; Art. 10(1)(e) bars customer personal data in the passport without explicit consent; toys: consumers cannot be required to register or use a password (Art. 20(4)), no tracking beyond need (Art. 20(10)); construction: different access levels (Art. 76(2)(f)).

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.mechanism: Integrity is where platforms differ most, and many vendor pages state no mechanism (Siemens, SAP, Kezzler, atma.io, TrusTrace, EON, Minespider, Tilkal, Cofinity-X, iPoint, Scantrust). Stated mechanisms: (1) Signed credentials: W3C verifiable credentials with issuer DID in the issuer field, product DID in credentialSubject and a proofValue made with the issuer key; verification fetches the issuer DID document from /.well-known/did.json (did:web); the write-up lists did:web limits (no traceable key rotation, trust rests on domain control). Transpareo's renderer verifies Data Integrity proofs in the visitor's browser with the cryptosuites eddsa-jcs-2022 and ecdsa-sd-2023, and uses a signed manifest naming each version with URL, hash and date. (2) Hash anchoring: Digimarc anchors a hash of each EPCIS event to IOTA through a blockchain integration hub, with event authors identified by DIDs and signatures as verifiable credentials; the ledger holds the hash, not the event. (3) Permissioned or public chains and tokens: Circulor on Hyperledger Fabric with smart contracts that validate supplier records; Arianee passports as NFTs on EVM chains (the docs read name no token standard); Circularise claims a public chain plus zero-knowledge proofs (secondary). (4) Process controls: audit logs with timestamp and actor (Circularise, Arianee), on-demand PDF reports said to carry cryptographic proof of authenticity (Circularise; scheme not stated), GPS and facial checks in the Circulor app (vendor claim). (5) Revocation: W3C Bitstring Status List v1.0 is a Recommendation; UNTP uses it for credentials. Law: Art. 11 points (g) and (h) require ensured authentication, reliability and integrity, and security, privacy and fraud avoidance; toys Art. 20(8)-(9); construction Art. 78(h)-(i). Law does not prescribe signatures, ledgers or tokens.

L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.observable_black_box: Presence and type of a proof (JWS compact, embedded proof object, anchor reference); issuer identifier and key location; verification result; status check; whether the document changes without a signature change.
L08_authentication_reliability_integrity.law_delta: Law states the goals (authentication, reliability, integrity) and leaves the mechanism open. The digital consistency of a signed passport does not prove that the signed attributes are true. Ledger anchoring, NFTs and zero-knowledge proofs are vendor choices; no adopted law or open standard in this file makes any of them mandatory.

L09_registry_and_customs.mechanism: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778: the registry has a secure user website, an API for registering passports and receiving registry information, a verification platform, a scheme generating unique registration identifiers, storage for identifiers and commodity codes, a list of verified DPP service providers, a semantic repository, a log system and identification and authorisation schemes (Art. 3, prior record; points (b), (c), (d), (e), (f) re-read today). The Commission checks structure, granularity, commodity codes and the link to the back-up; it does not check substantive correctness (recital 16). The registration identifier is returned through the same channel as the upload (recital 15); each new version links back to the original identifier (recital 18); the operator or a third party acting for it can request a downloadable proof of registration valid 90 days (recital 17); the operator stays liable when a third party registers (recital 31); operators are verified with eIDAS-based means such as qualified signatures, seals or attestations (Art. 4, as summarised from the text read). Service providers are named as an actor to be identified by verification (recital 4). Platforms: Spherity advertises registry registration support and back-up services; the CIRPASS-2 service provider response lists registration as a possible provider service and asks whether providers may batch registrations (OBADA/Kron comment). Customs: toys require the operator to upload the unique product and operator identifiers to the registry before placing the toy on the market (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509, Art. 22(1)), the registry issues a registration identifier (Art. 22(2)), and customs release for free circulation needs that identifier and a commodity code check against the registry, done electronically (Art. 23); the recitals say the registry is to be linked to the EU customs system CSW-CERTEX (recital 57).

L11_roles_and_governance.mechanism: Roles in law: the economic operator is responsible for the passport; the DPP service provider is an independent third party authorised by that operator that processes passport data to make it available (Art. 2(32)); providers are not economic operators (Art. 2(46), prior record); a provider may not sell, reuse or process the data beyond the service unless the operator agrees (Art. 11, second subparagraph); the Commission may set requirements for becoming a provider, a certification scheme where appropriate, and service requirements (Art. 11, third subparagraph) and may set procedures for digital credentials of operators (fourth subparagraph, optional, none located). Status on 2026-10-19: the Commission DPP page lists the delegated act for DPP service providers under Q2 2027 (heading 'DPP requirements for construction products and service providers') and under Q3 2027 (heading 'DPP requirements for service providers'); no adopted act or draft text was located; the Have Your Say page for initiative 14382 returned only a heading to the fetch tool. A secondary explainer (infodpp.eu) reports a call for evidence in November to December 2024 and a public consultation from 8 April to 1 July 2025 with 275 valid responses and a Commission factual summary Ares(2025)6861790 (not retrieved). The CIRPASS-2 consortium response (December 2024) is a collection of diverging opinions: it separates providers of the mandatory back-up from other providers, asks for service level and recovery objectives, warns that provider metadata about reads and writes has commercial value, and some contributors want ISO/IEC 27001 as a baseline. Construction: requirements for providers and an optional certification scheme will come from the delegated act under Regulation (EU) 2024/3110, Art. 75(2)(g), based on Regulation (EU) 2024/1781 where possible. Toys: Art. 21(5) applies provider requirements; Art. 19(11) makes the manufacturer or provider show a Safety Gate link when the passport is accessed. Batteries: the Commission FAQ says the Batteries Regulation does not define the provider as a distinct actor (prior record). Governance models on platforms: Catena-X has an operating company (Cofinity-X) and certified solution providers (certification tied to named releases Jupiter and Saturn); tyre industry proposes GDSO as a possible provider (search excerpt); EBSI and eIDAS 2.0 business wallet appear in Spherity and Protokol statements; UNTP is a UN/CEFACT trust protocol with pilot status. Literature on data governance (10.1177/17835917231152799, 10.1007/s43615-026-01102-y) treats governance as under-specified.

end_to_end_flows.name: Platform-hosted passport with GS1 Digital Link QR, independent back-up and registry registration (composite of vendor and law statements)
actors: DPP platform or service provider (primary host)
steps: 1. The operator loads product data into the platform from ERP, PLM or PIM systems and supplier inputs, at model, batch or item level.

2. The platform issues identifiers; for GTIN products it builds a GS1 Digital Link URL https://<domain>/01/<GTIN>[/10/<lot>][/21/<serial>] and generates QR codes (Arianee batch endpoint POST /v2/qr-codes/batch is one example).
3. A tag or label supplier prints or encodes the carrier; some platforms use dynamic serialized QR so the redirect can change later.
4. The operator makes a back-up copy available through an independent DPP service provider (Art. 10(4)) and records the provider reference (Annex III first paragraph point (l)).

5. The operator or a verified third party registers the passport in the registry through the website or API; the registry checks structure, granularity, commodity code and the back-up link, then returns a registration identifier (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1778, Art. 8 and recitals 14 to 16).
6. A scan sends an HTTPS request to the printed URL; a conformant resolver redirects to the default link or answers by linkType, Accept and Accept-Language; unknown valid identifiers give 404.
7. The platform serves the public view; restricted fields need a role (token, credential or contract) and are filtered per audience.
8. Later events (repair, resale, recycling) are added by authorised actors; a remanufactured product gets a new passport linked to the original (Art. 11 point (d)).
9. If the operator ceases activity, access moves to the back-up copy by whatever redirect design applies; adopted law does not fix that design.

end_to_end_flows.name: Catena-X dataspace provision and consumption of a battery or product passport
actors: Eclipse Dataspace Connectors on both sides
steps: 1. The provider obtains a Business Partner Number and Catena-X credentials through onboarding (Cofinity-X ECOPASS page).

2. The provider registers a digital twin (AAS shell) in the Digital Twin Registry and attaches the passport submodel conforming to an aspect model such as io.catenax.generic.digital_product_passport 6.1.0 or io.catenax.battery.battery_pass 6.1.0 (EcoPass KIT adoption view).
3. The Industry Core Hub creates the EDC asset and access policy automatically when a submodel is attached (README description).
4. The consumer discovers the partner endpoint, sends a catalog request and negotiates a data contract through its connector.
5. The consumer retrieves the submodel through the data plane and renders it; the retired Tractus-X DPP application did this for batteries by QR code or manufacturer and battery id.
6. Ownership and access rights are enforced by the connector policy; no further verification mechanism is named on the pages read.

end_to_end_flows.name: Verifiable-credential passport with did:web (Spherity battery write-up)
steps: 1. The manufacturer hosts a DID document at https://<domain>/.well-known/did.json for the issuer DID did:web:<domain>.
2. A product DID of the form did:web:<domain>/battery/<UUID> identifies the passport; its DID document has service endpoints to a human-readable page and to the machine-readable credentials.
3. The passport data is issued as a W3C verifiable credential; issuer holds the company DID, credentialSubject holds the product DID and the data, proofValue holds the signature.
4. The QR code carries the DID plus a resolver link.

5. A verifier resolves the DID through a DID resolver (hosted or self-hosted), reads the service endpoint, fetches the credential, gets the issuer public key from the issuer DID document and checks the signature; schema conformance is checked separately against the vocabulary.
6. Public attributes are open; other attributes need user authentication, which the write-up calls non-standardised and shows only as a mock-up.

end_to_end_flows.name: EPCIS 2.0 lifecycle events with ledger anchoring (Digimarc blueprint)
steps: 1. A stakeholder records an event (for example module replacement) in a mobile web app after login; events enter an EPCIS 2.0 API.
2. The event is signed with the author's DID as a verifiable credential using IOTA identity tooling.
3. The integration hub writes only a hash of the event to the IOTA ledger.
4. A GS1 Digital Link identity resolves through Digimarc Engage to experiences such as authenticity check or recycling instructions.
5. The verifier web app uses the tangle.js SDK to compare platform data with the ledger hashes and signatures.

end_to_end_flows.name: Back-up redirect when the operator ceases activity (CIRPASS-2 options, option 1)
actors: Commission or other fallback redirection services
steps: 1. The registry holds, per passport, the link to the primary data source and the link to the back-up data source.
2. A DPP-aware client that cannot reach the primary asks a fallback redirection service for the back-up link and fetches the back-up copy.
3. A generic web browser scanning the printed URL does not fail over by itself; contributors accept this as a con of option 1.

4. Other options differ: subdomain control by the Commission with DNS redirect, central redirect, agency takeover of domains, or two URLs with a fixed mapping. The paper records opinions only and does not state a legal choice.

end_to_end_flows.name: Toy passport registration and customs check (Regulation (EU) 2025/2509)
actors: toy manufacturer or operator placing on the market
steps: 1. The manufacturer creates the passport before placing the toy on the market (Art. 19(1)); it covers one toy model and includes at least Part I of Annex VI (Art. 19(2)(a), (c)).
2. The operator makes a back-up copy available through a passport service provider (Art. 19(13)).
3. Before placing on the market the operator uploads the unique product and operator identifiers to the registry (Art. 22(1)); the registry returns a registration identifier (Art. 22(2)).
4. For import, the declarant gives the registration identifier (Art. 23(2)); customs release follows an electronic check of identifier and commodity code against the registry (Art. 23(3), (4)).
5. When the passport is accessed, the manufacturer or provider displays a link to the Safety Gate reporting section (Art. 19(11)).

failure_modes.fault: Batch or model level URL (GTIN only, or GTIN plus lot) is printed on the product but the platform resolves only the item form.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Resolve each granularity of the same GTIN and compare status codes.

failure_modes.fault: Qualifier order is wrong (serial before lot) or a GTIN-12 is not padded to 14 digits in the path.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Parse the carrier URL against the GS1 syntax rules; request the URL.

failure_modes.fault: Dynamic QR redirect points to a vendor domain that the operator does not control; the carrier breaks when the vendor contract ends.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Follow the redirect chain and compare the registered domain of each hop with the operator domain.

failure_modes.fault: The QR code is decodable but the decoded text differs from the identifier in the passport.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Decode the image and compare with the passport identifier (identifier.consistency).

failure_modes.fault: A valid identifier with no data returns 200 with an empty page instead of 404.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Request a freshly generated unused identifier and inspect status.

failure_modes.fault: Content negotiation ignored: Accept application/ld+json returns HTML or a different document than JSON.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Request with several Accept values and compare media type and body.

failure_modes.fault: Redirect loop or long chain between resolver, platform and back-up host.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Bounded redirect following with a hop count.

failure_modes.fault: DELETE removes a passport immediately without archive state, losing history.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Create, delete, then read versions and archive state on a sandbox.

failure_modes.fault: Webhook or event endpoint accepts unauthenticated posts.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Send an event without credentials to a sandbox; expect 401 or 403.

failure_modes.fault: Document references a demo or unreachable @context or schema that is not an official one.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare @context entries with a pinned allowlist.

failure_modes.fault: Units or code lists drift from the pinned sector model (for example free-text unit instead of codelist).
failure_modes.detectable_by: JSON Schema or SHACL validation with rule pack ranges and units.

failure_modes.fault: Back-up copy is hosted by the same provider as the primary, so one failure removes both.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare hosting domains and the provider reference in passport and registry; manual review of the contract.

failure_modes.fault: Older versions disappear after an update, or retention shorter than the sector period.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Repeated acquisition and date-query reads against the declared update rule.

failure_modes.fault: Restricted fields leak through search results, export files, error messages or the HTML page while the JSON view hides them.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Synthetic canary values in restricted fields and a probe of every channel per role.

failure_modes.fault: Consumer view demands registration or a password (toys) or tracks usage beyond need.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Anonymous request of the public URL; inspection of redirects to login and tracking calls.

failure_modes.fault: Signature valid but issuer key not tied to the operator (did:web on an unrelated domain) or key rotated without history.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare issuer DID host with the operator host; verify with a trust bundle.

failure_modes.fault: Passport changes after anchoring but the anchor or hash is not recomputed.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Recompute the hash of the fetched document and compare with the anchored value.

failure_modes.fault: A 'verified' badge is rendered from a server flag, not from a check of the proof.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Tamper with a sample document and see whether the badge changes (client-side behavior).

failure_modes.fault: Registration identifier shown in the passport does not exist in the registry, or the back-up link differs from the registered one.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Compare passport fields with the mock registry record.

failure_modes.fault: A remanufactured product gets a new passport with no link to the original.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Check link fields between the pair; data.rules relationship rule.

failure_modes.fault: Provider reuses or sells passport data or usage metadata beyond the service.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Not black-box testable; manual review of contract and terms, signed as manual evidence.

failure_modes.fault: A vendor presents an own certification as the ESPR provider certification scheme.
failure_modes.detectable_by: Manual review of claims against the status of the delegated act (not adopted on 2026-10-19).
